tools.whatItDoes: Graphical link-analysis tool that maps relationships between people, domains, emails, IPs and companies from public data.
Modular OSINT framework (Metasploit-style console) that gathers domains, hosts, contacts and credentials from public sources.
Search engine for internet-connected devices; finds exposed servers, webcams, ICS and their open ports and banners.
Search engine for internet hosts and TLS certificates; similar to Shodan, strong for certificate and subdomain discovery.
Collects emails, subdomains, hosts and employee names from search engines and public sources.
Fingerprinting Organization with Collected Archives: downloads public documents from a site and extracts metadata (usernames, software, paths).
Looks up domain registration: registrant, contacts, name servers, dates.
Queries DNS records (A, MX, NS, TXT) and can attempt zone transfers.
Port scanner: discovers hosts, open ports, services, versions and OS. NSE scripts add vulnerability checks. Key flags: -sS, -sT, -sU, -sV, -O, -A, -Pn, -p, -T0-5, --script=vuln.
Commercial vulnerability scanner (Tenable) that finds known CVEs, missing patches and misconfigurations.
Free, open-source vulnerability scanner (Greenbone); the open alternative to Nessus.
Web server scanner that checks for dangerous files, outdated server software and misconfigurations. Noisy, not stealthy.
Automates finding and exploiting SQL injection, including dumping database contents.
Checks systems against SCAP security baselines and compliance profiles (e.g. STIG, CIS).
Black-box web app scanner that fuzzes pages for injection, XSS and file inclusion flaws.
Scanner for WordPress sites: finds vulnerable plugins, themes and weak user accounts.
Static code analysis scanner for Ruby on Rails applications.
Offline password cracker for many hash types; dictionary, brute-force and rule-based modes.
GPU-accelerated offline hash cracker; the fastest option for large hash lists.
Online brute-force tool that guesses logins against live services (SSH, FTP, HTTP forms, RDP, SMB).
Parallel online login brute-forcer, similar to Hydra.
Modular, multi-purpose online brute-forcer with fine control over responses.
Custom Word List generator: crawls a target website and builds a wordlist from its words.
Legacy Windows tool for sniffing, ARP poisoning and recovering/cracking passwords.
Extracts plaintext passwords, hashes and Kerberos tickets from Windows memory (LSASS); enables pass-the-hash and golden-ticket attacks.
Older Java GUI tool for brute-forcing web directories and file names with a wordlist.
Intercepting web proxy: captures, modifies and replays HTTP requests; includes scanner, Repeater and Intruder. Community edition is free.
Zed Attack Proxy: free, open-source intercepting proxy and web vulnerability scanner; the open alternative to Burp.
Fast command-line brute-forcer for web directories, files, DNS subdomains and virtual hosts.
Web Application Attack and Audit Framework: finds and exploits web app flaws.
API client for building and sending requests; used to test REST and SOAP APIs, including mobile app back ends.
Exploitation framework with thousands of exploits, payloads (e.g. Meterpreter) and post-exploitation modules.
Command-line search of a local copy of Exploit-DB to find public exploits for a given software version.
PowerShell/Python post-exploitation and command-and-control framework.
.NET command-and-control (C2) framework for red teams, managed through a web interface.
Maps Active Directory relationships as a graph to find attack paths to Domain Admin.
Poisons LLMNR, NBT-NS and mDNS on a local network to capture NTLM password hashes.
Python library and scripts for Windows network protocols (SMB, Kerberos); includes psexec.py, secretsdump.py, ntlmrelayx.py.
Swiss-army tool for Active Directory: password spraying, credential checking and command execution across many hosts.
Abuses IPv6 DHCP on Windows networks to become the DNS server and relay credentials.
Scans Git repositories and code for leaked secrets such as API keys and passwords.
Sysinternals tool that runs commands on remote Windows hosts; used for lateral movement and living off the land.
Wi-Fi toolkit: airmon-ng (monitor mode), airodump-ng (capture), aireplay-ng (deauth/injection), aircrack-ng (crack WEP/WPA keys).
Passive wireless detector and sniffer; finds networks (including hidden ones) and devices.
Automates Aircrack-ng and Reaver attacks against nearby Wi-Fi networks.
Brute-forces the WPS PIN to recover a WPA/WPA2 passphrase.
Runs evil-twin attacks against WPA2-Enterprise to capture credentials.
Wi-Fi stress and attack tool: deauthentication floods, beacon floods, SSID brute-forcing.
Python GUI Wi-Fi cracker for WEP/WPA/WPS.
Spoofs or clones Bluetooth device names, classes and addresses.
Wireless Geographic Logging Engine: public crowdsourced map of Wi-Fi networks; used for wardriving recon.
An unauthorized AP set up to lure clients (evil twin); built with tools like hostapd.
Builds phishing emails, credential-harvesting clone sites and malicious payloads for social engineering tests.
Browser Exploitation Framework: hooks a victim's browser via a JavaScript snippet, then runs commands through it.
Fake caller ID for vishing (voice phishing) tests.
Reads/writes raw TCP/UDP: banner grabbing, file transfer, bind and reverse shells.
Nmap project's modern Netcat with SSL and proxy support.
Encrypted remote shell; also used for port forwarding and tunneling through a pivot host.
Forces a program's traffic through a chain of proxies (e.g. SOCKS via a pivot) to reach internal networks or hide origin.
GUI packet capture and protocol analyzer.
Crafts custom TCP/UDP/ICMP packets for firewall testing, port scans and DoS testing.
Python library for crafting, sending and decoding packets.
On-path (MITM) attack tool: ARP poisoning, sniffing and traffic manipulation.
Disassembler/decompiler that turns compiled binaries into readable assembly for analysis.
Command-line debugger for Linux programs; steps through code and inspects memory.
Windows debugger popular for exploit development (buffer overflows), with Python scripting.
Older 32-bit Windows debugger for reverse engineering binaries.
Microsoft's Windows debugger for user-mode and kernel-mode code and crash dumps.
Automated static and dynamic analysis of Android and iOS apps.
Android security framework that probes an app's exposed components (activities, content providers) for flaws.
Dynamic instrumentation toolkit: injects scripts into running apps to hook functions and bypass checks.
Built on Frida; runtime mobile exploration, e.g. bypassing SSL pinning and root/jailbreak detection.
Official Android tools such as adb, used to install, debug and interact with apps on a device or emulator.
Decompiles Android APK files into Java source.
IDE for decompiling, editing and recompiling Android APKs.
Command-line tool that hides (and extracts) data inside JPEG, BMP, WAV and AU files, with optional password.
GUI tool for hiding data in images and adding invisible watermarks.
Hides messages in text files using trailing whitespace (spaces and tabs).
Converts an image into sound, so a picture appears in the audio's spectrogram.
Audio analysis tool; viewing a spectrogram reveals images or data hidden in sound.
Reverse image search; finds the original of an image to compare against a possibly altered copy.
Multi-cloud auditing tool that reviews AWS, Azure and GCP configurations for security risks.
AWS exploitation framework (Rhino Security Labs) for attacking misconfigured AWS accounts, e.g. IAM privilege escalation.
Finds a company's cloud resources (storage buckets, apps) across providers by brute-forcing names.
Policy-as-code engine that checks and auto-fixes cloud resources against rules.
Provider command-line tools and libraries (AWS CLI, az, gcloud) used to interact with cloud APIs during a test.
Fast, free GUI scanner that sweeps IP ranges for live hosts and open ports.
Open-source web application vulnerability scanner.
Command-line auditor for AWS (also Azure/GCP) security best practices and compliance (CIS, PCI).
Command-line packet capture to .pcap files.
Public database for checking whether an IP has been reported for malicious activity.
Scans a file, hash, URL or domain against dozens of antivirus engines and threat feeds.
Pulls readable text out of a binary file; quick first look at suspected malware (URLs, commands).
Commercial malware sandbox that detonates files and reports their behavior.
Open-source malware sandbox that runs files in a VM and logs what they do.
Collects and correlates logs from across the network and raises alerts.
Runs automated response playbooks on alerts (e.g. block an IP, isolate a host).
Endpoint Detection and Response agent that monitors hosts and can isolate or remediate them.
